items.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I mean he is in the pure tradition of the great tenor saxophone like Coleman Hawkins, Don Byas, Lucky Thompson...

ctx.x: I had to insist but I don’t know, I know what to say, that in some ways it was one more time that little voice that told me it’s the moment to push a little bit.
I mean he is in the pure tradition of the great tenor saxophone like Coleman Hawkins, Don Byas, Lucky Thompson, you can really feel the deep sounds in him.

I’ll tell you a story. A few weeks after that, one of the shows that was supposed to be performed with my trio and Johnny Griffin and Guy, of course Guy was just a few days before going to pass away. And I still had that concert to play with Griff. So I remember I was down by his house in the middle of the west part of France. So I go to Griff’s house. And he said, I stayed at his house, and he said, “Okay tomorrow we take my wife’s car and you and I will drive to the concert.” And when we got there we were…
